clue.text: Part of London law I stop breaking

indicators.note: breaking suggests the letters of 'law I stop' are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone vows to give up breaking the law.
explanation.walkthrough: Plaistow is a district of East London, in the borough of Newham.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaistow is a district in the East London borough of Newham.

clue.text: Tapir running around spies female

indicators.note: a creature running around is all over the place, so the letters of 'Tapir' are jumbled

parts.note: the CIA is the American spy agency

explanation.surface: A tapir scampers about near some secret agents and a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Patricia is a woman's given name, so it can stand for a female.

clue.text: American ensign leaves base with company going round independent island capital

indicators.note: in a down clue the base is the bottom letter, so the flag word loses its last letter

parts.note: a jack is a ship's flag or ensign

indicators.note: going round means the company letters enclose the next piece

explanation.surface: A US flag is lowered and a military company circles an independent island's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Ajaccio is the chief city of Corsica, a French Mediterranean island.

clue.text: This probably contains letter run off after lead evens out

indicators.note: after puts the eloping word at the end, following the jumbled letters
out signals that the letters of 'lead evens' are disordered

parts.note: to elope is to run off secretly to marry

explanation.surface: A letter runs off once a lead is levelled out, like a race narrative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges LEAD EVENS into the first nine letters; ELOPE follows. The definition is a playful description: a closed paper wrapper usually holds a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A gummed paper cover that has been closed is the usual home of a posted letter.

clue.text: A pious lot cross about liquid lunch?

indicators.note: about signals the letters are turned around and rearranged

parts.note: a cross is the shape of the letter X

explanation.surface: A devout group, angry, goes off for a boozy lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' jumbles A PIOUS LOT together with X (cross). A 'liquid lunch' usually means drinks instead of food; here it is literally a liquid dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A broth made from beef tail is a lunch you drink rather than chew, punning on the boozy phrase.

clue.text: Cool hip clubs around St Paul's?

indicators.note: around suggests the letters of 'Cool hip clubs' are moved about

explanation.surface: Trendy nightclubs cluster around St Paul's Cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: St Paul's looks like the London cathedral, but it is also a fee-paying school in London; the question mark marks it as an example. In Britain a 'public school' is an elite private school.
explanation.definitionFit: St Paul's School in London is an example of an elite fee-paying British independent school.

clue.text: Went under it — a mess

indicators.note: making a mess of the letters of 'under it a' rearranges them

explanation.surface: Someone crawled underneath it, and the result was a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went' is a euphemism: to go is to relieve oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphemistically, to 'go' is to relieve oneself, so passing water fits.

clue.text: Russell possibly told stories about having drawn comparisons

indicators.note: about means the fibbing word goes around the director's first name

parts.note: to tell stories is to lie, so it gives lied
Ken Russell was a British film director; 'possibly' marks him as an example of a Ken

explanation.surface: A man named Russell is accused of making things up about comparisons he drew.
explanation.definitionFit: To compare one thing to another is to say it resembles that thing.

clue.text: Intelligent third party suffering reverse

parts.note: C is the third letter of the alphabet

indicators.note: suffering a reverse means the party word is turned backwards

parts.note: a revel is a lively party

explanation.surface: A bright outsider in a dispute suffers a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'third party' looks like one idea, but 'third' gives C and 'party' gives REVEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever and intelligent are synonyms, both meaning quick-witted.

clue.text: Internally split, still backing US right-wingers

indicators.note: internally means the next piece goes inside the other
backing means the word for still is read backwards

parts.note: yet can mean still, as in 'yet more'
apart means split up or separated

explanation.surface: A divided political movement still supports the American right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'split' reads as a verb about the movement, but it is the adverb 'apart'. 'backing' turns the still-word round, and 'Internally' puts the split-word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tea Party is a conservative American political movement on the Republican right.

clue.text: Bow down in case Kim is executing leaders

indicators.note: the leaders of the words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Bow down in case Kim Jong-un executes you.
explanation.walkthrough: A dickie bow is the British name for a bow tie.
explanation.definitionFit: A dickie bow is the British informal name for a bow tie, so the word alone can mean that tie.

clue.text: Having funds incorporated with resistance to change

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for resistance
to edit is to change a text

explanation.surface: A wealthy company is resistant to change.
explanation.definitionFit: An account that is in credit holds a positive balance, so the holder has money.

clue.text: Between Portugal and Spain, find a strange new tribe

indicators.note: between puts the jumbled letters inside the two country codes

parts.note: P is the international vehicle code for Portugal
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters of 'a new' are oddly arranged

explanation.surface: On the Iberian border someone discovers an unknown tribe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pawnee are a Native American people of the Great Plains.

clue.text: Essex town goat eats heather

indicators.note: eats means the goat word takes the plant word inside it

parts.note: a billy is a male goat
erica is the botanical name for heather

explanation.surface: A goat in an Essex town munches heather.
explanation.walkthrough: Billericay is a town in Essex, a county north-east of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Billericay is a commuter town in the English county of Essex.

clue.text: Party held by the Italian star

indicators.note: held by means the party word sits inside the Italian article

parts.note: il is Italian for 'the'
a do is a party

explanation.surface: An Italian star throws a party.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is a celebrated, adored figure, much like a star.

clue.text: Rejecting mines, finishes making allowances

indicators.note: rejecting means turning back, so the mines word is read backwards

parts.note: pits are mines
ends are finishes

explanation.surface: A miner turns down the pits and wraps up his pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Stipends are fixed regular payments, like a salary or allowance.

clue.text: See 3
Monster's head replaced by offensive figure

indicators.note: head replaced by means the first letter of the monster word is swapped for the offensive

parts.note: a dragon is a mythical monster
the Tet Offensive was a 1968 campaign in the Vietnam War

explanation.surface: A monster's head is swapped for an offensive image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' looks like an adjective but is the Tet Offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetragon is a four-sided geometric shape, a quadrilateral.

clue.text: Leave nut to get cracked later

indicators.note: cracking a nut breaks it up, so the letters of 'Leave nut' are rearranged

explanation.surface: Leave the nut to be cracked another time.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventual describes what happens in the end, at some future point.

clue.text: See 20
City where I've left carrot for a singer

indicators.note: for means the carrot word takes the place of the 'a' in the city

parts.note: Geneva is a Swiss city
the letter a as written in the clue

indicators.note: left means the letters of 'I've' depart from the carrot word

parts.note: a carrot is an incentive, as in carrot and stick
the letters I, V, E of 'I've'

explanation.surface: In a city someone abandons a carrot meant for a singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' strips I, V, E from INCENTIVE to leave INCENT, which replaces the A of GENEVA ('for a').
explanation.definitionFit: Gene Vincent was an American rockabilly singer, famous for Be-Bop-A-Lula.

clue.text: Hat being the wrong way up is mark of snobbery

indicators.note: in a down clue the wrong way up reads the hat word from bottom to top

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat
M is the abbreviation for the German mark

explanation.surface: Wearing a hat upside down is a sign of being a snob.
explanation.definitionFit: Elitism is the belief in a superior group, much like snobbery.

clue.text: Beat marines surrounding Cinque Port pointlessly

indicators.note: surrounding means the marines letters go around the port

parts.note: RM is the abbreviation for Royal Marines

indicators.note: pointless means without a compass point, here E for east

parts.note: Hythe in Kent is one of the Cinque Ports

explanation.surface: Marines beat round a historic Kentish port to no purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cinque Ports are a historic group of south-east English coastal towns, Hythe among them.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhythm is a regular beat in music or speech.

clue.text: See 5
Great king welcomes new famine

indicators.note: welcomes means the new letter is taken inside

parts.note: huge means great
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A great monarch greets a fresh famine.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunger is a want of food, the condition suffered in a famine.

clue.text: Row about Astley possibly gets more complicated

indicators.note: about means the row word goes around the singer's name

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
Rick Astley is a British pop singer; 'possibly' marks him as an example of a Rick

explanation.surface: A dispute over Rick Astley grows more involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel, but it is a row of seats, a tier.
explanation.definitionFit: Trickier means harder to handle, i.e. more intricate.

clue.text: Bloke's planetary explorer comes back on time

definitions.note: 'Bloke's' reads as 'bloke is', a man's name being a bloke

indicators.note: in an across clue on means placed after, so the reversed explorer follows the time letter
comes back means the explorer word is read backwards

parts.note: a rover is a vehicle exploring a planet such as Mars

explanation.surface: A man's Mars rover returns on schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: Trevor is a common British man's first name, so it can stand for a bloke.

clue.text: Pain keeps Bill's partner moving quickly

indicators.note: keeps means the pain word holds the partner word inside

parts.note: a sting is a sharp pain
coo partners bill in the phrase 'bill and coo'

explanation.surface: A painful sting has Bill's partner rushing about.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like a man, but in 'bill and coo', the lovers' cooing, his partner is COO.
explanation.definitionFit: Scooting means dashing or darting off fast.

clue.text: Doctor finally breaks children's joints

indicators.note: breaks means the letter breaks into the children word

parts.note: mites are small children

indicators.note: finally picks the final letter of Doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor at last fixes children's joints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'children's joints' reads as body parts, but mites are children and the joints are carpentry ones.
explanation.definitionFit: A mitre is a corner joint in woodwork made with angled cuts.

clue.text: Father irritated many keeping Liberal Democrat in order

indicators.note: keeping means the jumbled letters hold the next piece inside
irritated suggests the letters of 'many' are stirred up
in means the party letters go inside the order letters

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit
LD is the abbreviation for Liberal Democrat

explanation.surface: Dad annoyed lots of people by keeping a Lib Dem in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irritated' rearranges 'many' so that it wraps the Lib Dem letters already held inside the Order of Merit; 'in order' looks like 'tidily' but is that honour.
explanation.definitionFit: My old man is informal British slang for one's dad.
